sources.entry: Spree Commerce - Spree is a complete, modular & API-driven open source e-commerce solution for Ruby on Rails. (Demo, Source Code) BSD-3-Clause Ruby

summary.one_liner: Spree is an open-source, API-driven e-commerce platform for Ruby on Rails with a REST API, TypeScript SDKs, a React admin dashboard, and a Next.js storefront.
summary.what_it_does: Spree provides a complete REST API for storefronts, admins and sellers, with publishable and scoped secret keys, rate limiting, and an OpenAPI 3.0 spec, plus TypeScript SDKs. It includes a Vite + React admin dashboard and a matching Seller Panel for marketplace vendors. A Next.js 16 storefront with multi-region routing, Stripe payments, and customer accounts is available as an optional part of the setup. Core commerce features described in the README include B2B price lists and companies, marketplace seller onboarding with per-seller order splitting and commissions, promotions and gift cards, multi-location inventory, and tax handling via Avalara and Stripe Tax. A local MCP server and a Spree CLI are offered for managing stores through chat or the terminal.
use_cases: run B2B and wholesale sales channels
manage an online store via AI agents or chat
how_to_run: Deploy backend via official Docker images or Dockerfiles
Deploy Next.js storefront to Vercel, Netlify, or any Node.js host
notable: Modular, API-driven commerce core with REST API, OpenAPI 3.0 spec and TypeScript SDKs
Built-in multi-vendor marketplace with seller onboarding, order splitting and Stripe Connect payouts
B2B features: price lists with volume tiers, companies with locations, customer groups, catalogs
Local MCP server and agent skills for managing a store via AI assistants
Official Docker images for deployment on any Docker-compatible host
caveats: Multi-tenant SaaS, B2B approval workflows, marketplace Shopify/WooCommerce sync, audit logging and SLA support require the paid Enterprise Edition
Hosting platforms named in the README are examples of Docker-compatible hosts; the storefront is a separate Node.js deployment
